newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian coffee bean exports rise in June.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian coffee bean exports rise in June.

text.p: Ivorian robusta coffee bean exports rose to 31,215 tonnes in June, almost twice as high as June 1996 exports and the busiest month so far in the 1996/7 (Oct-Sept) season, official shipping data show.
The data showed 24,300 tonnes of June 1997 exports went from the main port of Abidjan and 6,915 tonnes from San Pedro.
Coffee product exports, from Abidjan, included 949 tonnes of soluble coffee.
Cumulative bean exports in the first nine months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season totalled 121,093 tonnes against 114,078 tonnes by the same period in 1995/96.
Ivorian bean exports got off to a late start in 1996/97 after low world prices in late 1996, tighter bank lending policies to exporters and quality problems slowing grading.
Exports have picked up over the past couple of months.
June coffee exports are the highest on a monthly basis since the opening of the 1996/97 season, which has yielded Ivory Coast's largest crop since the early 1980s.
Ivory Coast exported 15,970 tonnes of robusta coffee beans in June 1996 and 20,527 tonnes the year before.
Upcountry buyers say the 1996/97 season is effectively over, with less than 1,000 tonnes of coffee reaching ports each week.
Grading of remaining stocks was continuing, they said.
Arrivals by late July stood at almost 310,000 tonnes, compared to a total 1995/96 crop of 180,000 tonnes, leaving large stocks still unshipped.
